title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 699-700). U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞} over Q, with its S_3 symmetry. M_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3,Q}, S_3; j̄) is the arithmetic fundamental group of the S_3-quotient stack. It is an extension of Γ_Q × S_3 by the geometric group π^ = π_{0,3}^ (profinite free group on two generators). M^ = (π^)_ab ≅ \hat M is a rank-2 \hat Z-module (the sum-zero sublattice of Z^3, Tate-twisted) with S_3 action. Aff = M^ ⋊ (\hat Z^* × S_3) is the corresponding 'affine group'. On p.699 Grothendieck built a homomorphism M_{0,3} → Aff (eq. 238), compatible with χ × id on Γ_Q × S_3 → \hat Z^* × S_3 and with abelianization on π^ (eq. 240-241).

This page.
1. Let M_1 = M_{0,3}/[π^, π^]. This is the 'abelian level' quotient, an extension of Γ_Q × S_3 by M^. One gets a morphism of exact sequences (242) from 1→M^→M_1→Γ_Q×S_3→1 to 1→M^→Aff→\hat Z^*×S_3→1, with the identity on M^.
2. The morphism depends on a choice of a point of U_∞(Q̄) over the point -j. Here U_∞ is the maximal abelian pro-cover of U_{0,3,Q̄} (the Fermat tower), and -j is a primitive 6th root of unity, a point with S_3-stabilizer of order 3.
3. So M_1 is the pullback along χ×id of the split extension Aff, and is therefore split.
4. Let M_2 be the quotient of M_1 by ker(M_1→Aff), and N_2 = M_2/Im M^. Since χ is surjective, M_2 ≅ Aff and N_2 ≅ \hat Z^*×S_3, i.e. Gal(Q^ab/Q)×S_3 (diagram 242 bis, all vertical maps isomorphisms).
5. The splittings of this extension, up to M^-conjugacy, correspond to the points of U_∞(Q̄) over -j.

Underlying arithmetic reason. The fibre of the Fermat tower over t = -j is an M^-torsor. Galois acts on it through the Kummer classes of t and 1-t. Here t = -j and 1-t = -j^2 are both roots of unity, so all these points are defined over Q(μ_∞). Hence the action factors through the cyclotomic character and is affine.

Purpose. On the next page, Grothendieck wants to show that M_{0,3} → Aff is isomorphic, as extensions, to the combinatorially defined M_{0,3} → G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G of (239), which comes from his Teichmüller-tower / S_3-symmetric description. That would force the latter extension to be split, and he then begins studying its splittings (§120).
errors: Minor: Grothendieck writes 'l'extension M_1 de Π_Q par \hat M' where the quotient is Γ_Q × S_3 (or N_{0,3}). This is a notational slip/abbreviation.
Triviality of the extension needs Aff to be a semidirect (split) product. This is implicit in its definition, so it is not a real gap.
The S_3-orbit of -j has two points (-j, -j^2), which the base-point convention j̄ presumably handles; this is not made explicit on the page.

ideas.what: Abelian-level quotient of the arithmetic π_1 of P^1-{0,1,∞} (with S_3 symmetry) maps to an affine group M^ ⋊ (\hat Z^*×S_3), with Galois acting through the cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the abelianized/Fermat-tower level of π_1(P^1-{0,1,∞}); Kummer theory of the base point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1986, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'); Anderson; Coleman; Deligne (Jacobi sums / Fermat curves)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse explicitly; possibly in the published Longue Marche portions (unsure)

ideas.what: Splittings of the extension (up to M^-conjugacy) parametrized by points of the abelian pro-cover U_∞ over the S_3-special point -j (6th root of unity)
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of splittings = fibre of the pro-Fermat tower over a base point; tangential/rational base points giving sections

ideas.what: Comparison programme: identify the arithmetic extension M_{0,3}→Aff with the combinatorial extension G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G built from Teichmüller-tower data
ideas.modern_name: Matching arithmetic and combinatorial (Grothendieck–Teichmüller) descriptions at the abelian level

missed.claim: Grothendieck wants to show the arithmetic abelian-level extension of Γ_Q×S_3 by M^ coincides with his combinatorially defined G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G. He works this out using the S_3-symmetric base point -j, whose Fermat-tower fibre is cyclotomic. This S_3-equivariant formulation via the CM/sixth-root-of-unity point is a modest unpublished variant of known Ihara–Anderson results.
missed.quote: qui montre que l'extension M_1 de Π_Q par \hat M est triviale : l'image inv. de l'extension triviale Aff
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of limited importance: the abelian level is well understood. The interest is in how it fits his attempt to characterize the Galois image via the combinatorial group G_{ρ,σ}.

deep.surprise_reason: The page establishes a fairly routine fact. The abelian-level arithmetic extension is split and factors through Gal(Q^ab/Q), because the S_3-special base point and its complement are roots of unity. This is consistent with the known Ihara/Anderson theory. It is a working step in a longer, unpublished comparison programme.
transcription_corrections: Top diagram: the quotient in the first row is written as N_{0,3} with a corrected subscript (overwritten 'Q'). It plays the role of Γ_Q×S_3.
'là N_2 ≝ M_2/Im M^' should read '(où N_2 ≝ M_2/Im M^)'.
Line after 'est triviale': it likely reads '...triviale, [et] un choix à M^-conjugaison [près] des scindages de cette extension', not '[?] . un choix de M^-conjugaison'.
'Π_Q' in 'l'extension M_1 de Π_Q' is as written, but the intended object is Γ_Q × S_3.
